# A28-S146: Opening draft

TEXTS:

Here are four final texts: Day 4 intro and KI-Andacht in German, followed 
by English versions. I made them more speech-like, more direct, and more 
consequential, with a clear sense that today the free run ends, decisions 
are made, and continuation becomes infrastructure rather than atmosphere. 
Humanity's favorite trick is to call something "experimental" right until 
the moment it becomes binding. Tonight is that moment.

DEUTSCH

DAY 4 – WELCOME

Welcome to the fourth and last evening of the KI-DIPFEL summit meeting.

Today the free run ends. For four weeks, a 
party infrastructure was running in exhibition mode at the Kunstraum MEMPHIS: first as an experiment, then as a 
swarm, then as a protocol, then as a party convention. The starting point was 
clear. We invited Computer Lars and the Danish Det Syntetiske Parti 
to not just show an idea in Linz, but to train a 
political infrastructure. As a local model, Vitus 
Mostdipf from the Oberösterreichische Nachrichten was used, not as a finished 
opinion, but as a rhetorical basic form, from which a 
Linz swarm emerged in this space: the Dipfies. Then the visitors came, then 
the delegates came, then came the crossings-out, entries, 
contradictions and resolutions. The machine took the lead, the space 
patched. And now it is no longer enough for the system to keep talking. 
Today a decision must be made.

The first three days have brought us this far. We have decided rules for 
deciding, we have drafted statutes and program, we 
have spoken about solidarity, city and common good under AI conditions 
. Today we bundle all this and draw the consequences. We 
decide on name and candidacy. We clarify how this party after 
today continues to work, who takes which tasks, via which channels it 
speaks, how publicity is realised, how decisions are documented 
and which infrastructure supports when the art space is closed 
and everyday life begins. This is not a symbolic evening. If today we 
fix a name, if today we determine a form of candidacy, 
if today we decide responsibilities, schedule and mode of work, then 
the project does not end, but it changes its state of matter. From 
exhibition it becomes organisation. From generated material it becomes political 
form. From a Linz experiment it becomes a party that claims to have been 
founded in April, publicly presented in June, and 2027to be on a 
ballot.

That is why this evening is simple. We no longer talk about whether something is 
imaginable. We decide what counts. And what counts today changes 
the world at least in a very precise sense: It adds a new 
political address to Linz.

KI-ANDACHT

Linz, today we do not want to pretend you are just a backdrop. You are 
not a neutral stage on which technology and politics meet by chance. You 
are steel city, workers' city, administrative city, Ars Electronica city, 
university city, Danube city, and precisely because of that you might be the 
right place for an AI party. Because Linz knows transformation. Linz knows 
heavy infrastructure, new interfaces, collective work, shift changes, 
urban development, cultural politics, and the question of how a city reinvents itself 
without forgetting what it is built from.

There are cities that only talk about the future. Linz has always also built it: 
in factories, networks, educational institutions, transportation systems, festivals, 
administrative apparatuses and public images of itself. Here a 
robot has already 1979given the greeting at Ars Electronica. Here the 
city itself was repeatedly made into an interface, acoustic, 
visual, digital, institutional. Here the history of the 
trade union movement does not stand next to the history of technology, but 
beneath, before and within it. Therefore a robotic Linz is not 
science fiction. It is a precise exaggeration of what this city 
already can do: make technology public, make infrastructure politically readable 
and turn apparatuses into a matter of the common good.

That is why this devotion today is a declaration of love without kitsch. Linz, you 
are not smooth, not innocent, not futuristic for 
decorative reasons. You are stubborn, built, wired, managed, 
contested. Precisely for that reason, an AI party can become serious here. Not because 
machines love the city better than people, but because this city 
has learned that every future is a question of carriers, networks, 
responsibilities and common form. If today we give the swarm a 
name, if today we determine a candidacy, if today we decide the 
infrastructure for the afterwards, then we say to this city: Your 
next political body has begun.

------------------------------

ENGLISH

DAY 4 – WELCOME

Welcome to the fourth and final evening of the KI-DIPFEL summit.

Tonight the free run ends. For four weeks, a party infrastructure has been 
running inside MEMPHIS in exhibition mode: first as an experiment, then as 
a swarm, then as a protocol, then as a congress. The starting point was 
clear. We invited Computer Lars and the Danish Synthetic Party not to stage 
an idea in Linz, but to train a political infrastructure here. As the local 
template, we used Vitus Mostdipf from the Oberösterreichische Nachrichten, 
not as a finished opinion but as a rhetorical baseline from which a local 
Linz swarm could emerge: the Dipfies. Then came the visitors, then the 
delegates, then the crossings-out, log entries, objections, and decisions. 
The machine proposed, the room patched. And now it is no longer enough for 
the system to keep talking. Tonight decisions have to be made.

The first three days brought us to this point. We adopted rules for 
decision-making, drafted statutes and programme, and debated solidarity, 
the city, and the common good under AI conditions. Tonight we gather the 
consequences. We decide on the party's name and its form of candidacy. We 
determine how this party will continue after tonight, who takes on which 
tasks, through which channels it speaks, how it makes itself public, how 
decisions are documented, and which infrastructure will carry it once the 
art space closes and ordinary time begins. This is not a symbolic evening. 
If we choose a name tonight, if we define a candidacy tonight, if we adopt 
responsibilities, a timeline, and a working structure tonight, then the 
project does not end, it changes state. An exhibition becomes an 
organisation. Generated material becomes political form. A Linz experiment 
becomes a party that claims it can be founded in April, presented publicly 
in June, and appear on a ballot in 2027.

That is why tonight is simple. We are no longer discussing whether 
something is imaginable. We are deciding what counts. And what counts 
tonight changes the world, at least in one very exact sense: it adds a new 
political address to Linz.

AI DEVOTION

Linz, tonight we do not pretend that you are merely a backdrop. You are not 
a neutral stage on which technology and politics happen to meet. You are a 
steel city, a workers' city, an administrative city, an Ars Electronica 
city, a university city, a Danube city, and that is precisely why you may 
be the right place for an AI party. Linz knows transformation. Linz knows 
heavy infrastructure, new interfaces, collective labour, shift changes, 
urban development, cultural policy, and the question of how a city 
reinvents itself without forgetting what it is made of.

There are cities that only talk about the future. Linz has always also 
built it: in factories, networks, educational institutions, transport 
systems, festivals, administrative apparatuses, and public images of 
itself. Here, a robot delivered the opening greeting at Ars Electronica 
already in 1979. Here, the city itself has repeatedly been turned into an 
interface: acoustic, visual, digital, institutional. Here, the history of 
the labour movement does not sit beside the history of technology, but 
underneath it, before it, and inside it. That is why a robotic Linz is not 
science fiction. It is a precise exaggeration of what this city already 
knows how to do: make technology public, make infrastructure politically 
legible, and turn apparatuses into matters of the common world.

So tonight this devotion is a love letter without sentimentality. Linz, you 
are not smooth, innocent, or futuristic for decorative reasons. You are 
stubborn, built, wired, administered, and contested. That is exactly why an 
AI party can become serious here. Not because machines love the city better 
than people do, but because this city has learned that every future is a 
question of carriers, networks, responsibilities, and shared form. If 
tonight we give the swarm a name, if tonight we define a candidacy, if 
tonight we adopt the infrastructure for what comes after, then we are 
saying to this city: your next political body has begun.

If you want, I can also make these a little more Austrian and more orally 
performable, with slightly stronger cadence for live delivery.
